warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Keswick Campsite
warnings.description: The heavy rain and strong winds from Storm Boelo have now left the area, but river and lake levels remain high. Further showers are expected today, Tuesday 27 October 2026. Locations most affected will be Keswick Campsite flooding from the lake and the River Greta. We continue to closely monitor the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: The north Norfolk coast at Salthouse and east Cley
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: The north Norfolk coast at Salthouse and east Cley
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning. 

Flooding is expected from 5:00am to 9:00am Wednesday 28th October 

Locations most affected will be Coast Road in Salthouse and, Coast Road in Cley. Flooding is also expected for Salthouse and Cley marshes. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Wells of 3.92mAODN at 7:00am, on Wednesday 28th October, which is 0.67m above tide tables, Wind Force 5, South-Westerly. The high tide tomorrow evening is not expected to reach Flood Warning. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   

This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: The north Norfolk coast at Wells Quay
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: The north Norfolk coast at Wells Quay
warnings.description:
Higher than normal tides are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning. 

Flooding is expected from 5:00am to 9:00am Wednesday 28th October. 

Locations most affected will be The Quay, East End and roads joining the Quay between the Flood Barrier and East End including, Unns Yard, Jicklings Yard, Staithe Street, Croft Yard and Standard Street. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Wells of 3.92mAODN at 7:00am, on Wednesday 28th October, which is 0.67m above tide tables, Wind Force 5, South-Westerly. The high tide tomorrow evening is not expected to reach Flood Warning. 

We are closing flood gates . 

Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   

This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: South Hayling and South Eastoke seafront
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: South Hayling and South Eastoke seafront
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding on Wednesday.
Flooding is expected for 2 hours either side of Wednesday afternoon's tide at 12:21 on 28/10/2026.  
The weather increases tide table values by 0.22 m. Total forecast tide is 5.23 metres Chart Datum (2.50 mAOD) at Portsmouth. Light Westerly Force 3 wind. South Hayling beach (towards Eastoke) has been affected by previous storms. Water could push further up the beach than normal. Property at Eastoke corner, near the nature reserve, and at Southwood Road may flood. Overtopping of splash walls along the beach front may flood gardens. Beach huts at West Beach, near the Inn on the beach, may also be affected. Thursday's tide at 00:45 on 29/10/2026 is forecast to be 50 cm lower (2 mAOD).
We are liaising with emergency services and local authorities .
Activate any flood protection products you may have.  
This message will be updated by 4:00PM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.description: High tides and forecast weather conditions are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning. Flooding is expected from 05:30 to 08:30 on 28/10/2026. High astronomical tides and a large surge is expected. The wind direction is predominantly offshore, so the main risk is from higher than normal water levels. Locations most affected will be coastal roads, promenades and footpaths. We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.
